denial.label: Pre-existing disease waiting period not completed

grounds: Essential hypertension was first diagnosed on 2023-12-17, AFTER the policy start date 2023-08-24; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal against Denial D03 – Pre‑existing Disease Waiting Period Not Completed (Claim ID: 8a378120-cbc8-8dc0-5bef-9aa0feb91936)

Claim Details:  
Patient Name: Santa Labadie  
Patient ID: 8a378120-cbc8-8dc0-04be-44a8c807932f  
Date of Service: 2024-01-16  
Encounter Class: AMB (Follow‑up encounter)  
Diagnosis: Essential hypertension (onset 2023-12-17)  
Procedure Category: Cardiac  
Plan: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Plan Code SGH‑GOLD)  
Coverage Start Date: 2023-08-24  
Total Claim Amount: INR 342.20  

Grounds for Appeal:  
Essential hypertension was first diagnosed on 2023‑12‑17, which is after the policy start date of 2023‑08‑24. According to the policy definition, a condition first diagnosed on or after the policy start date is not a Pre‑Existing Disease and therefore the Pre‑Existing Disease waiting period does not apply [suraksha_gold_policy#5]. Consequently, the denial based on a waiting period is inconsistent with the policy’s own waiting‑period clause, which applies only to conditions meeting the Pre‑Existing Disease definition [suraksha_gold_policy#10].

Clinical Necessity:  
Monitoring of essential hypertension after diagnosis or a medication change is medically necessary to prevent serious complications such as stroke, heart failure and kidney disease. The clinical guideline recommends review every 4–6 weeks until control is achieved and then every 3–6 months, including blood pressure measurement, electrolytes, creatinine and screening for target‑organ damage [hypertension#3]. The follow‑up encounter submitted in this claim fulfills these clinical monitoring requirements.

Reference to Denial Standards:  
Under the insurer’s denial standards, the burden of proof for any exclusion or waiting‑period denial rests with the insurer, which must provide documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed before the policy start date [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6]. The insurer has not supplied such evidence. Moreover, the insured has the right to appeal this denial in writing within the stipulated period, identifying the claim, denial reason, policy clauses and supporting clinical evidence, as we are doing now [claims_procedure_and_grievance#8].

Request:  
In view of the above, we respectfully request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be reprocessed, and the amount of INR 342.20 be paid in full to the provider.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Gold Family Floater Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (Clause 2.2) are covered after 24 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Essential Hypertension — Diagnosis and Monitoring > Medical Necessity of Monitoring
citations.quote:
## Medical Necessity of Monitoring
After diagnosis or a medication change, review every 4–6 weeks until controlled, then every 3–6 months. Monitoring includes blood pressure measurement, electrolytes and creatinine, and screening for target-organ damage (ECG, urine albumin). Regular monitoring prevents stroke, heart failure and kidney disease.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C4. Appeals and Grievances > C4.1 Right to Appeal
citations.quote:
## C4. Appeals and Grievances  
### C4.1 Right to Appeal
The insured, or the provider on the insured's behalf, may appeal a denial in writing within 30 days of the denial letter. The appeal should identify the claim, the denial reason, the policy clauses relied upon and the supporting clinical evidence.
